provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft; host source restrictions and execution verification

draft_notes.explanation: The family recolours every small object. An object here is a single-colour, 4-connected component of non-background cells. If it has 1 or 2 cells, it becomes the marker colour (original 3). Objects with 3 or more cells stay unchanged. 4-connectivity and component size do not change under rotation or reflection, so the emitted program works directly in visible coordinates with no axis-specific logic. The colour roles are specialized as constants: the background is palette[0], because the generator skips exactly colour 0 rather than the most common colour, and the marker is palette[3]. Adjacent cells of different non-background colours are treated as separate objects, matching the generator's same-colour flood fill.
draft_notes.limitations: This assumes the background is always original colour 0 (palette[0]), as in the generator. It does not use the archived solver's most-common-colour heuristic, which could fail when non-zero cells are the majority. Demonstrations are not consulted. I have not run any tests.
